name: implied_vs_realized_vol_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when VIX has spiked intraday but 20-minute realized volatility has not kept pace, market makers who sold calls into the fear spike are over-hedged short-delta and will buy the index to unwind as VIX begins to revert. We detect this regime by computing the intraday VRP (VIX/100 minus 20-min annualized realized vol) and z-scoring it over the trailing 60-minute window; when VRP z-score exceeds 1.5 and VIX's 5-minute rate-of-change turns negative (confirming the spike is reversing), NIFTY tends to drift upward 15-25 spot points over the following 30-90 seconds as dealer delta hedges unwind. The short leg fires when RV exceeds implied vol (VRP z-score < -1.5) with VIX rising, signaling complacency before a move.

indicators.name: rv_240
indicators.purpose: 240 bars = 20 minutes of realized vol. The original used 5-day RV to characterize structural regime; we adapt to intraday because a session fear spike and compression can unfold within an hour. 20 minutes is long enough to be statistically meaningful (240 log-return samples) yet recent enough to reflect current regime.

indicators.name: vrp
indicators.purpose: Variance risk premium: implied vol (VIX) minus realized vol. Positive VRP means options are expensive relative to recent actual movement — dealers are over-hedged and will need to unwind.

indicators.name: vrp_z
indicators.purpose: Z-score over 720 bars = 60 minutes. The original z-scored over 20 days (~7,500 1-min bars). We compress to 60 minutes because intraday VRP dynamics are driven by intraday flow — a spike that is extreme relative to the past hour is actionable, but that same spike may look unremarkable vs 20-day history. 60 minutes balances enough history to define 'extreme' while staying within the current session's volatility context.

indicators.name: vix_roc_60
indicators.purpose: VIX % change over the last 60 bars = 5 minutes. This is the TRIGGER: a declining VIX over 5 minutes after a spike confirms fear is compressing, not escalating. 5 minutes filters out noisy 5-30 second VIX fluctuations while being fast enough to enter early in the compression move. Original used a 60-minute (60-bar 1-min) ROC; we scale to 5 minutes to match our 30-120 second hold time.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 36 bars = 3-minute RSI. The original used RSI(30) on 1-min bars = 30-minute RSI to confirm NIFTY was oversold. We compress to 3 minutes because we hold 30-120 seconds — we need current momentum confirmation, not whether NIFTY was sold off over the past 30 minutes. RSI < 45 on 3-min bars confirms spot is in a short-term pullback within the VIX spike, making the VRP compression bounce thesis actionable.

conditions: vrp_z > 1.5 (VRP is 1.5 std above 60-min mean — implied vol significantly exceeds realized)
vix_roc_60 < -0.02 (VIX has declined >2% in last 5 minutes — fear spike reversing)
rsi_36 < 45 (NIFTY spot in 3-min pullback — entering on weakness, not chasing)
buy_ce.confirmation: All three conditions simultaneously true; no CE position already open

conditions: vrp_z < -1.5 (RV significantly exceeds implied vol — complacency, market underpricing risk)
vix_roc_60 > 0.02 (VIX rising — implied vol catching up to realized, risk-off)
buy_pe.confirmation: All three conditions simultaneously true; no PE position already open

exit.stop_rationale: 5 option points = ~10 NIFTY spot points adverse move. If NIFTY drops 10 spot pts while we're in a CE trade, the VRP compression thesis is wrong — fear is escalating, not abating. Per CONVENTIONS Table 10.4, a 2-minute hold sees typical moves of 5-10 option pts; a 5pt stop positions us just inside the expected noise band, cutting losers where the thesis clearly failed.
exit.target_rationale: 8 option points = ~16 NIFTY spot points. VIX-compression bounces on NIFTY historically travel 15-25 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds as dealer delta unwinds accumulate. Capturing 16 spot pts (about 60% of the lower end of the range) at delta ~0.5 gives 1:1.6 risk-reward. Per Table 10.4, 2-minute NIFTY moves average 5-10 option pts; 8 pts targets the upper-middle of this range.

filters.vix_filter: VIX must be above 12 for buy_ce signals (VRP only meaningful when VIX is above baseline); above 10 for buy_pe (complacency matters less in low-vol regimes)
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST (skip first 15 minutes to allow VRP baseline to establish over 720 bars)
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume is sufficient throughout session
filters.trend_filter: none explicit — VRP regime filter subsumes trend context

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — intraday VRP z-score normalization is noisier than 20-day normalization; signal frequency higher but quality lower than original

adaptation_notes: Key changes from original: (1) Lookback compressed from 20-day/5-day RV windows to 60-min/20-min intraday windows — the structural VRP persists in the original because retail option sellers supply IV; intraday we target the SAME mechanism but scoped to the current session's fear spike. (2) RSI lookback compressed from 30 min (30 1-min bars) to 3 min (36 5-sec bars) because our hold time is 30-120 seconds, not 60-300 minutes. (3) Direction logic preserved: elevated VRP → buy CE (fear will compress, NIFTY recovers); negative VRP → buy PE (complacency before drop). This is opposite to iv_dislocation_v1 which buys PE on high IV — the distinction is VIX DIRECTION CONFIRMATION (declining VIX → CE, rising VIX → PE) which aligns the signal with the index direction being traded.
weaknesses: Intraday VRP z-score over 60 minutes is much noisier than 20-day z-score — false signals will be higher
India VIX computation has known staleness issues (NSE computes every minute, not every 5 seconds) — vix_df may have repeated values, making ROC signal less reliable
Low-frequency signal from original (0-1/day) becomes a medium-frequency signal (1-4/day) by compressing lookbacks — but the compression may lose the structural VRP property
Does not work on BANKNIFTY because India VIX is based on NIFTY options only
